newsitem.title: FRANCE: French cabinet member says get ready to go to Zaire.
newsitem.headline: French cabinet member says get ready to go to Zaire.

text.p: A French cabinet member called on Paris' European partners on Sunday to be prepared to intervene to prevent a human disaster in Zaire.
"We (France) are already pre-positioning supplies, food, water, shelters and clothing," Secretary of State for emergency humanitarian action Xavier Emmanuelli told TF-1 television.
"But France cannot act alone. Everyone in other European capitals must now start preparing to act as soon as the opportunity presents itself.

"The European community, the international community, must intervene in the framework of a mandate, a mandate that will come from a political gathering, a United Nations mandate for example," he said.
Officials said the French government was waiting to see whether African heads of state, due to discuss the Zaire fighting at a meeting in Nairobi on Tuesday, call for action by the European Union.

The Foreign Ministry said minister Herve de Charette discussed Zaire in separate telephone calls in the past few hours with U.N. Secretary-General Boutros Boutros-Ghali, Irish Foreign Minister Dick Spring, whose country holds the rotating EU presidency, and European Union commission president Jacques Santer.

"These talks were aimed at examining the situation in Kivu province and seeing how the international community can reply to the urgency of the humanitarian drama developing there," a Foreign Ministry statement said.
Emmanuelli earlier confirmed Paris was considering a European plan to open "humanitarian corridors" in Zaire to help masses of refugees threatened by ethnic fighting.
The well-informed daily Le Monde said on Saturday that the European Union was thinking of opening "humanitarian corridors" protected by troops in Zaire to help refugees.
The report said such an operation might involve French, Belgian and South African troops.
Italy said on Saturday that "suitable measures of protection" were needed so the United Nations could aid refugees in eastern Zaire.
Emmanuelli said there was "absolute urgency to get a humanitarian rescue underway."
He said supplies were available both in the region and ready to be moved there from Europe "but the problem is to deliver them into this zone of chaos".

Most aid agencies have pulled out of east Zaire, where they were helping about a million Rwandan Hutu refugees trapped by fighting between the Zairean army and ethnic Tutsi rebels backed by the Tutsi-led Rwandan army.
France sent troops to halt civil strife in Rwanda in 1994 and is still smarting under accusations that its intervention was mostly aimed at advancing French policy objectives.
